q: The ratio between the length and the breadth of a rectangular park is 3 : 2. If a man cycling along the boundary of the park at the speed of 12 km/hr completes one round in 8 minutes, then the area of the park (in sq. m) is:
s: Perimeter = Distance covered in 8 min. Perimeter = $$\left( {\frac{{12000}}{{60}} \times 8} \right){\text{m}}$$ Perimeter = 1600 m Let length = 3x metres and breadth = 2x metres. Then, 2(3x + 2x) = 1600 or x = 160 Therefore Length = 480 m and Breadth = 320 m Therefore Area = (480 x 320) m 2 = 153600 m 2

q: An error 2% in excess is made while measuring the side of a square. The percentage of error in the calculated area of the square is:
s: 100 cm is read as 102 cm. ∴ A 1 = (100 x 100) cm 2 and A 2 (102 x 102) cm 2 (A 2 - A 1 ) = [(102) 2 - (100) 2 ] = (102 + 100) x (102 - 100) = 404 cm 2 ∴ Percentage error $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{404}}{{100 \times 100}} \times 100} \right)\% \\ & = 4.04\% \end{aligned}$$

q: The ratio between the perimeter and the breadth of a rectangle is 5 : 1. If the area of the rectangle is 216 sq. cm, what is the length of the rectangle?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{2\left( {l + b} \right)}}{b} = \frac{5}{1} \\ & \Rightarrow 2l + 2b = 5b \\ & \Rightarrow 3b = 2l \\ & b = \frac{2}{3}l \\ & {\text{Then,}} \\ & {\text{Area = }}216\,c{m^2} \\ & \Rightarrow l \times b = 216 \\ & \Rightarrow l \times \frac{2}{3}l = 216 \\ & \Rightarrow {l^2} = 324 \\ & l = 18\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: The percentage increase in the area of a rectangle, if each of its sides is increased by 20% is:
s: Let original length = x metres and original breadth = y metres $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Original}}\,{\text{are}} = \left( {xy} \right){m^2} \\ & {\text{New}}\,{\text{length}} = \left( {\frac{{120}}{{100}}x} \right)m = \left( {\frac{6}{5}x} \right)m \\ & {\text{New}}\,{\text{breadth}} = \left( {\frac{{120}}{{100}}y} \right)m = \left( {\frac{6}{5}y} \right)m \\ & {\text{New}}\,{\text{area}} = \left( {\frac{6}{5}x \times \frac{6}{5}y} \right){m^2} = \left( {\frac{{36}}{{25}}xy} \right){m^2} \\ & {\text{The}}\,{\text{difference}}\,{\text{between}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{original}}\,{\text{area = }}xy \\ & {\text{and}}\,{\text{new}}\,{\text{area}}\,\frac{{36}}{{25}}xy\,{\text{is}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{36}}{{25}}} \right)xy - xy \\ & = xy\left( {\frac{{36}}{{25}} - 1} \right) \\ & = xy\left( {\frac{{11}}{{25}}} \right)\,or\,\left( {\frac{{11}}{{25}}} \right)xy \\ & \therefore {\text{Increase}}\,\% \\ & = \left( {\frac{{11}}{{25}}xy \times \frac{1}{{xy}} \times 100} \right)\% \\ & = 44\% \end{aligned}$$

q: A rectangular park 60 m long and 40 m wide has two concrete crossroads running in the middle of the park and rest of the park has been used as a lawn. If the area of the lawn is 2109 sq. m, then what is the width of the road?
s: Area of the park = (60 x 40) m 2 = 2400 m 2 Area of the lawn = 2109 m 2 ∴ Area of the crossroads = (2400 - 2109) m 2 = 291 m 2 Let the width of the road be x metres. Then, 60 x + 40 x - x 2 = 291 ⇒ x 2 - 100 x + 291 = 0 ⇒ ( x - 97)( x - 3) = 0 ⇒ x = 3 m

q: The diagonal of the floor of a rectangular closet is $$7\frac{1}{2}$$ feet. The shorter side of the closet is $$4\frac{1}{2}$$ feet. What is the area of the closet in square feet?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Outer}}\,{\text{Side}} \\ & = \sqrt {{{\left( {\frac{{15}}{2}} \right)}^2} - {{\left( {\frac{9}{2}} \right)}^2}ft} \\ & = \sqrt {\frac{{225}}{4} - \frac{{81}}{4}ft} \\ & = \sqrt {\frac{{144}}{4}ft} \\ & = 6ft \\ & \therefore {\text{Area}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{closet}} = \left( {6 \times 4.5} \right)sq.\,ft = 27\,sq.\,ft. \end{aligned}$$

q: A towel, when bleached, was found to have lost 20% of its length and 10% of its breadth. The percentage of decrease in area is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{original}}\,{\text{length}} = x\,{\text{and}} \\ & {\text{original}}\,{\text{breadth}} = y \\ & {\text{Decrease}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{area}} \\ & = xy - \left( {\frac{{80}}{{100}}x \times \frac{{90}}{{100}}y} \right) \\ & = {xy - \frac{{18}}{{25}}xy} \\ & = \frac{7}{{25}}xy \\ & \therefore {\text{Decrease}}\,\% = \\ & \left( {\frac{7}{{25}}xy \times \frac{1}{{xy}} \times 100} \right)\% \\ & = 28\% \end{aligned}$$

q: A man walked diagonally across a square lot. Approximately, what was the percent saved by not walking along the edges?
s: Let the side of the square(ABCD) be x metres. Then, AB + BC = 2x metres AC =$$\sqrt 2$$ x = (1.41x) m Saving on 2x metres = (0.59x) m $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Saving}}\,\% = \left( {\frac{{0.59x}}{{2x}} \times 100} \right)\% \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 30\% \,\left( {{\text{approx}}} \right) \end{aligned}$$

q: The diagonal of a rectangle is $$\sqrt {41}$$ cm and its area is 20 sq. cm. The perimeter of the rectangle must be:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \sqrt {{l^2} + {b^2}} = \sqrt {41} \\ & {\text{Also}},\,lb = 20 \\ & {\left( {l + b} \right)^2} = \left( {{l^2} + {b^2}} \right) + 2/b = 41 + 40 = 81 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {l + b} \right) = 9 \\ & \therefore {\text{Perimeter}} = 2\left( {l + b} \right) = 18cm \end{aligned}$$

q: What is the least number of squares tiles required to pave the floor of a room 15 m 17 cm long and 9 m 2 cm broad?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{largest}}\,{\text{tile}} = \\ & {\text{H}}{\text{.C}}{\text{.F}}{\text{.}}\,{\text{of}}\,1517\,cm\,{\text{and}}\,902\,cm = 41\,cm \\ & {\text{Area}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{each}}\,{\text{tile}} = \left( {41 \times 41} \right)c{m^2} \\ & \therefore {\text{Required}}\,{\text{number}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{tiles}} \\ & = {\frac{{1517 \times 902}}{{41 \times 41}}} \\ & = 814 \end{aligned}$$

q: The difference between the length and breadth of a rectangle is 23 m. If its perimeter is 206 m, then its area is:
s: We have: (l - b) = 23 and 2(l + b) = 206 or (l + b) = 103 Solving the two equations, we get: l = 63 and b = 40 ∴ Area = (l x b) = (63 x 40) m 2 = 2520 m 2

q: The length of a rectangle is halved, while its breadth is tripled. What is the percentage change in area?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{original}}\,{\text{length}} = x\,{\text{and}}\, \\ & {\text{Original}}\,{\text{breadth}} = y \\ & {\text{Original}}\,{\text{area}} = xy \\ & {\text{New}}\,{\text{length}} = \frac{x}{2} \\ & {\text{New}}\,{\text{breadth}} = 3y \\ & {\text{New}}\,{\text{area}} = \left( {\frac{x}{2} \times 3y} \right) = \frac{3}{2}xy \\ & \therefore {\text{Increase}}\,\% = {\frac{1}{2}xy \times \frac{1}{{xy}} \times 100} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 50\% \end{aligned}$$

q: The length of a rectangular plot is 20 metres more than its breadth. If the cost of fencing the plot @ 26.50 per metre is Rs. 5300, what is the length of the plot in metres?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{breadth}} = x\,{\text{metres}} \\ & {\text{Then,}}\,{\text{length}} = \,\left( {x + 20} \right)\,{\text{metres}} \\ & {\text{Perimeter}} = {\frac{{5300}}{{26.50}}} m = 200m \\ & \therefore 2\left[ {\left( {x + 20} \right) + x} \right] = 200 \\ & \Rightarrow 2x + 20 = 100 \\ & \Rightarrow 2x = 80 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 40 \\ & {\text{Hence,}}\,{\text{length}} = x + 20 = 60m \end{aligned}$$

q: A rectangular field is to be fenced on three sides leaving a side of 20 feet uncovered. If the area of the field is 680 sq. feet, how many feet of fencing will be required?
s: We have: l = 20 ft and lb = 680 sq. ft. So, b = 34 ft. ∴ Length of fencing = (l + 2b) = (20 + 68) ft = 88 ft.

q: A tank is 25 m long, 12 m wide and 6 m deep. The cost of plastering its walls and bottom at 75 paise per sq. m, is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Area}}\,{\text{to}}\,{\text{be}}\,{\text{plastered}} \\ & = \left[ {2\left( {l + b} \right) \times h} \right] + \left( {l \times b} \right) \\ & = \left\{ {\left[ {2\left( {25 + 12} \right) \times 6} \right] + \left( {25 \times 12} \right)} \right\}{m^2} \\ & = \left( {444 + 300} \right){m^2} \\ & = 744{m^2} \\ & \therefore {\text{Cost}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{Plastering}} \\ & = Rs.\,\left( {744 \times \frac{{75}}{{100}}} \right) \\ & = Rs.\,558 \end{aligned}$$

q: The length of a room is 5.5 m and width is 3.75 m. Find the cost of paving the floor by slabs at the rate of Rs. 800 per square metre.
s: Area of the floor = (5.5 × 3.75)m 2 = 20.625m 2 ∴ Cost of paying = Rs. (800 × 20.625) = Rs. 16500

q: An artist has completed one-fourth of a rectangular oil painting. When he paint another 100 square centimetres of the painting, he would complete three-quarters of the painting. If the height of the oil painting is 10 cm, determine the length (in cm) of the oil panting.
s: Let the area of the whole painting be x cm 2 Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{4}x + 100 = \frac{3}{4}x \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}x = 100 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 200 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Area of painting = 200 cm 2 And, Height = 10 cm Length of painting : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{200}}{{10}}} \right)cm \\ & = 20\,\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: The length of a rectangle is increased by 60%. By what percent would the width have to be decreased so as to maintain the same area ?
s: Let original length = x and original breadth = y Then, original area = xy New length : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{160x}}{{100}} \\ & = \frac{{8x}}{5} \end{aligned}$$ Let the new breadth = z Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{{8x}}{5} \times z = xy \\ & \Rightarrow z = \frac{{5y}}{8} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Decrease in breadth : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{3y}}{8} \times \frac{1}{y} \times 100} \right)\% \\ & = 37\frac{1}{2}\% \end{aligned}$$

q: The following squares represent the monthly income of two families If the monthly income of family A is Rs. 40000, the monthly income of family B is ?
s: $$\frac{{{\text{Monthly income of family A}}}}{{{\text{Monthly income of family B}}}}$$ $$= \frac{{{\text{Area of square A}}}}{{{\text{Area of square B}}}}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{{40000}}{x} = \frac{{{2^2}}}{{{3^2}}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{40000 \times 9}}{4}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow x = 90000 \end{aligned}$$

q: What will be the length of the diagonal of that square plot whose area is equal to the area of a rectangular plot of length 45 metres and breadth 40 metres ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Area :}} \\ & = \left( {45 \times 40} \right){m^2} \Leftrightarrow \frac{1}{2} \times {\left( {{\text{Diagonal}}} \right)^2} \\ & = 1800\,\,\,\, \Leftrightarrow \,\,\,\,{\text{Diagonal}} \\ & = 60\,\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: Twenty-nine times the area of a square is one square metre less than six times the area of the second square and nine times its side exceeds the perimeter of other square by 1 metre. The difference in the sides of these squares is :
s: Let the sides of the two squares be x metres and y metres respectively Then, $$\Rightarrow 29{x^2} = 6{y^2} - 1.....(i)$$ And, $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 9x - 4y = 1 \\ & \Rightarrow 4y = 9x - 1 \\ & \Rightarrow y = \frac{{9x - 1}}{4}.....(ii) \end{aligned}$$ From (i) and (ii), we get : $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 29{x^2} = 6{\left( {\frac{{9x - 1}}{4}} \right)^2} - 1 \\ & \Rightarrow 29{x^2} = 6\left( {\frac{{81{x^2} + 1 - 18x}}{{16}}} \right) - 1 \\ & \Rightarrow 243{x^2} + 3 - 54x - 8 = 232{x^2} \\ & \Rightarrow 11{x^2} - 54x - 5 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {x - 5} \right)\left( {11x + 1} \right) = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 5\,\,m \\ & \therefore y = \frac{{9x - 1}}{4} = \frac{{9 \times 5\,\,m - 1}}{4} = 11\,\,m \\ & \text{Required difference} \\ & = \left(11-5\right) m \\ & = 6\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: In ∆PQR, side PQ = 3 cm and side PR = 25 cm. What is the area of ∆PQR ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Area of }}\Delta {\text{ }}PQR \\ & = \frac{1}{2} \times QR \times PQ \\ & {\text{Given}},\,PQ = 3\,cm \\ & QR = \sqrt {{{\left( {PR} \right)}^2} - {{\left( {PQ} \right)}^2}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \sqrt {{{\left( {25} \right)}^2} - {3^2}} \,cm \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \sqrt {625 - 9} \,cm \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \sqrt {616} \,cm \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 2\sqrt {154} \,cm \\ & \therefore {\text{Area}}\,{\text{of}}\,\Delta \,PQR \\ & = \left( {\frac{1}{2} \times 2\sqrt {154} \times 3} \right)c{m^2} \\ & = 3\sqrt {154} {\mkern 1mu} {\mkern 1mu} c{m^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: In an isosceles triangle, the measure of each of the equal sides is 10 cm and the angle between them is 45° . The area of the triangle is :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Area of the traingle :}} \\ & = \frac{1}{2}ab\sin \theta \\ & = \left( {\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 10 \times \sin {{45}^ \circ }} \right)c{m^2} \\ & = \left( {\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 10 \times \frac{1}{{\sqrt 2 }}} \right)c{m^2} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{50}}{{\sqrt 2 }} \times \frac{{\sqrt 2 }}{{\sqrt 2 }}} \right)c{m^2} \\ & = 25\sqrt 2 \,c{m^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: A triangle and a parallelogram are constructed on the same base such that their areas are equal. If the altitude of the parallelogram is 100 m, then the altitude of the triangle is :
s: Let the altitude of the triangle be h 1 and base of each be b. Then, $$\frac{1}{2}$$ × b 1 × h 1 = b × h 2 , where h 2 = 100 m ⇔ h 1 = 2 h 2 ⇔ h 1 = (2 × 100) m ⇔ h 1 = 200 m

q: The circumference of a circle, whose area is 24.64 m 2 , is :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \because \pi {R^2} = 24.64 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {R^2} = \left( {\frac{{24.64}}{{22}} \times 7} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow {R^2} = 7.84 \\ & \Leftrightarrow R = \sqrt {7.84} \\ & \Leftrightarrow R = 2.8\,m \\ & \therefore {\text{Circumference :}} \\ & = \left( {2 \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times 2.8} \right)m \\ & = 17.60\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: The ratio of the radii of two circle is 3 : 2. What is the ratio of their circumferences ?
s: Let the radii of the two circle be 3r and 2r respectively Then, required ratio : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{2\pi \left( {3r} \right)}}{{2\pi \left( {2r} \right)}} \\ & = \frac{3}{2} \\ & = 3:2 \end{aligned}$$

q: A circular grassy plot of land, 42 cm is diameter, has a path 3.5 m wide running around it outside. The cost of gravelling the path at Rs. 4 per square metre is :
s: Radius of the plot = 21 m Area of the path : $$\begin{aligned} & = \pi \left[ {{{\left( {24.5} \right)}^2} - {{\left( {21} \right)}^2}} \right]{m^2} \\ & = \left[ {\pi \left( {24.5 + 21} \right)\left( {24.5 - 21} \right)} \right]{m^2} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times 45.5 \times 3.5} \right){m^2} \\ & = 500.5\,{m^2} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Cost of gravelling : = Rs. (500.5 × 4) = Rs. 2002

q: A horse is tied at the corner of a rectangular field whose length is 20 m and width is 16 m, with a rope whose length is 14 m. Find the area which the horse can graze :
s: Required area = Area of the quadrant with radius 14 m : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times 14 \times 14 \times \frac{{90}}{{360}}} \right){m^2} \\ & = 154\,{m^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: A triangle with sides 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm is inscribed in a circle. The radius of the circle is :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & s = \frac{{13 + 14 + 15}}{2} = \frac{{42}}{2} = 21 \\ & \therefore \,\,\vartriangle = \sqrt {21 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \sqrt {s\left( {s - a} \right)\left( {s - b} \right)\left( {s - c} \right)} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \left( {2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 7} \right) \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 84\,c{m^2} \end{aligned}$$ Radius of circle : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{13 \times 14 \times 15}}{{4 \times 84}}} \right)c{m^2} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{65}}{8}} \right)cm \\ & = 8.125\,\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: A skating champion moves along the circumference of a circle of radius 28 m in 44 sec. How many seconds will it take her to move along the perimeter of a hexagon of side 48 m ?
s: Distance mode by the skater in 44 sec = Circumference of the circle = $$\left( {2 \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times 28} \right)$$ m = 176 m Speed of skater : = $$\left( {\frac{{176}}{{44}}} \right)$$ m/sec = 4 m/sec Perimeter of hexagon : = (6 × 48) m = 288 m ∴ Required difference : = $$\left( {\frac{{288}}{{4}}} \right)$$ sec = 72 sec

q: The diameter of a circle is equal to the perimeter of a square whose area is 3136 cm 2 . What is the circumference of the circle ?
s: Area of square = 3136 cm 2 Side of squared = $$\sqrt {3136}$$ = 56 cm Perimeter of square : = 4a = (4 × 56) cm = 224 cm = diameter of circle ∴ Circumference of circle : $$\begin{aligned} & = \pi d \\ & = \frac{{22}}{7} \times 224 \\ & = 704{\text{ cm}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The area of a rectangular field is 2100 sq. meters. If the field is 60 metres long, what is its perimeter ?
How many metres of carpet 63 cm wide will be required to cover the floor of a room 14 metres by 9 metres ?
s: Area of the floor = (14 × 9) m 2 = 126 m 2 ∴ Length of the carpet : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{126}}{{63}} \times 100} \right){\text{m}} \\ & = 200{\text{ metres}} \end{aligned}$$

q: If the length and breadth of a rectangular field are increased, the area increases by 50%. If the increase in length was 20 %, by what percentage was the breadth increased ?
s: Let the original length and breadth of the rectangle be l and b respectively Then, original area = lb New length = 120% of l = $$\frac{6l}{5}$$ New area = 150% of lb = $$\frac{3lb}{2}$$ New breadth : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{3lb}}{2} \times \frac{5}{{6l}}} \right) \\ & = \frac{{5b}}{4} \end{aligned}$$ Increase in breadth : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{5b}}{4} - b} \right) \\ & = \frac{b}{4} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Increase % : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{b}{4} \times \frac{1}{b} \times 100} \right)\% \\ & = 25\% \end{aligned}$$

q: Total area of 64 small squares of a chessboard is 400 sq. cm. There is 3 cm wide border around the chess board. What is the length of the side of the chess board ?
s: Area of each square : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{400}}{{64}}} \right)c{m^2} \\ & = 6.25\,c{m^2} \end{aligned}$$ Side of each small square : $$\begin{aligned} & = \sqrt {6.25} \,cm \\ & = 2.5\,cm \end{aligned}$$ Since there are 8 squares along each side of the chess board, we have : Side = [(8 × 2.5) + 6] cm = 26 cm

q: Area of a square natural lake is 50 sq. kms. A driver wishing to cross the lake diagonally, will have to swim a distance of :
s: Let the length of the diagonal be x km Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}{x^2} = 50 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} = 100 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 10\,{\text{km}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{10}}{{1.6}}} \right){\text{miles}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 6.25{\text{ miles}} \\ & \left[ {\because 1{\text{ mile}} = {\text{1.609 km}}} \right] \end{aligned}$$

q: A rectangular plank $$\sqrt 2$$ metre wide is placed symmetrically on the diagonal of a square of side 8 metres as shown in the figure. The area of the plank is :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ Let }}AP{\text{ }} = {\text{ }}AQ{\text{ }} = {\text{ }}x{\text{ metres}} \\ & {\text{Then,}} \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} + {x^2} = {\left( {\sqrt 2 } \right)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow 2{x^2} = 2 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} = 1 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 1\,m \\ & So,\,\,\vartriangle PAQ{\text{ is isosceles}}{\text{.}} \\ & \therefore PT = QT = \left( {\frac{{\sqrt 2 }}{2}} \right)m = \left( {\frac{1}{{\sqrt 2 }}} \right)m \\ & {\text{In }}\vartriangle {\text{ }}PTA{\text{, we have : }}\angle PTA = {90^ \circ } \\ & \therefore A{T^2} = A{P^2} - P{T^2} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = {1^2} - {\left( {\frac{1}{{\sqrt 2 }}} \right)^2} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 1 - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{2} \\ & Or,AT = \left( {\frac{1}{{\sqrt 2 }}} \right)m \\ & {\text{Similarly,}} \\ & CX = \left( {\frac{1}{{\sqrt 2 }}} \right)m \\ & \therefore PS = QR = XT \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = AC - 2 \times AT \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \left[ {8\sqrt 2 - \left( {2 \times \frac{1}{{\sqrt 2 }}} \right)} \right]m \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \left( {8\sqrt 2 - \frac{2}{{\sqrt 2 }}} \right)m \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{{14}}{{\sqrt 2 }}m \\ & {\text{Area of the plank :}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{14}}{{\sqrt 2 }} \times \sqrt 2 } \right){m^2} \\ & = 14\,{m^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: The area of a triangle whose sides are of lengths 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm is :
s: Since 3 2 + 4 2 = 5 2 , So it is a right-angled triangle with Base = 3 cm and Height = 4 cm ∴ Area : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 4} \right)c{m^2} \\ & = 6\,c{m^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: The perimeter of a triangle is 30 cm and its area is 30 cm 2 . If the largest side measures 13 cm, then what is the length of the smallest side of the triangle ?
s: Let the smallest side be x cm. Then, other sides are 13 cm and (17 - x) cm Let a = 13, b = x and c = (17 - x) So, s = 15 $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Area}} = \sqrt {s\left( {s - a} \right)\left( {s - b} \right)\left( {s - c} \right)} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \sqrt {15 \times 2 \times \left( {15 - x} \right)\left( {x - 2} \right)} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \sqrt {30\left( {15 - x} \right)\left( {x - 2} \right)} \\ & \therefore 30\left( {15 - x} \right)\left( {x - 2} \right) = {\left( {30} \right)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {15 - x} \right)\left( {x - 2} \right) = 30 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} - 17x + 60 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {x - 12} \right)\left( {x - 5} \right) = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 12{\text{ or }}x = 5 \\ & {\text{ Smallest side = 5 cm}} \end{aligned}$$

q: If a parallelogram with area P, a rectangle with area R and a triangle with area T are all constructed on the same base and all have the same altitude, then which of the following statements is false ?
s: Let each have base = b and height = h Then, P = b × h, R = b × h, T = $$\frac{1}{2}$$ × b × h So, P = R, P = 2T and T = $$\frac{1}{2}$$R, are all correct statements. ∴ Option B is false

q: The circumferences of two circle are 132 metres and 176 metres respectively. What is the difference between the area of the larger circle and the smaller circle ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 2\pi {R_1} = 132 \\ & \Rightarrow {R_1} = \frac{{132 \times 7}}{{2 \times 22}} \\ & \Rightarrow {R_1} = 21\,m \\ & \Rightarrow 2\pi {R_2} = 176 \\ & \Rightarrow {R_2} = \frac{{176 \times 7}}{{2 \times 22}} \\ & \Rightarrow {R_2} = 28\,m \\ & \therefore {\text{Required difference :}} \\ & = \pi \left( {R_2^2 - R_2^2} \right) \\ & = \pi \left( {{R_2} + {R_1}} \right)\left( {{R_2} - {R_1}} \right) \\ & = \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times 49 \times 7} \right){m^2} \\ & = 1078\,{m^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: The ratio of the radii of two circles is 1 : 3. Then the ratio of their areas is :
s: Let the radii of the two circle be r and 3r respectively. Then, required ratio : $$= \frac{{\pi {r^2}}}{{\pi {{\left( {3r} \right)}^2}}} = \frac{{\pi {r^2}}}{{9\pi {r^2}}} = 1:9$$

q: The circumference of a circular ground is 88 metres. A strip of land, 3 metres wide, inside and along the circumference of the ground is to be levelled. What is the budgeted expenditure if the levelling costs Rs. 7 per square metre ?
s: Let the radius of the ground be R metres. Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 2\pi R = 88 \\ & \Rightarrow R = \left( {\frac{{88 \times 7}}{{2 \times 22}}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow R = 14\,m \end{aligned}$$ Area of land strip : $$\begin{aligned} & = \pi \left[ {{{\left( {14} \right)}^2} - {{\left( {11} \right)}^2}} \right]{m^2} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times 25 \times 3} \right){m^2} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{1650}}{7}} \right){m^2} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Cost of levelling : $$\begin{aligned} & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {\frac{{1650}}{7} \times 7} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. 1650}} \end{aligned}$$

q: If the circumference of a circle is 100 units, then what will be the length of the arc described by an angle of 20 degrees ?
s: $$2\pi r = 100$$ So, length of the arc : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{2\pi r\theta }}{{360}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{100 \times 20}}{{360}}} \right){\text{units}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{50}}{9}} \right){\text{ units}} \\ & = 5.55{\text{ units}} \end{aligned}$$

q: If in a triangle, the area is numerically equal to the perimeter, then the radius of the inscribed circle of the triangle is :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Radius}} = \frac{{{\text{Area}}}}{{{\text{Semi - perimeter}}}} \\ & {\text{Radius}} = \left( {{\text{Area}} \times \frac{2}{{{\text{Area}}}}} \right) \\ & {\text{Radius}} = 2 \end{aligned}$$

q: Two equal circle are drawn in square in such a way that a side of the square forms diameter of each circle. If the remaining area of the square is 42 cm 2 , how much will the diameter of the circle measure ?
s: Let length of each side of square = 2π According to the question, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{\pi {r^2}}}{2} + \frac{{\pi {r^2}}}{2} + 42 = {\text{Area of square}} \\ & \Rightarrow \pi {r^2} + 42 = 4{r^2} \\ & \Rightarrow 4{r^2} - \pi {r^2} = 42 \\ & \Rightarrow {r^2}\left( {4 - \frac{{22}}{7}} \right) = 42 \\ & \Rightarrow {r^2}\left( {\frac{{28 - 22}}{7}} \right) = 42 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{6{r^2}}}{7} = 42 \\ & \Rightarrow {r^2} = \frac{{42 \times 7}}{6} \\ & \Rightarrow {r^2} = 7 \times 7 \\ & \Rightarrow r = 7 \\ & \therefore 2r = 14\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: The base of triangle is 15 cm and height is 12 cm the height of another triangle of double the area having base 20 cm is :
s: Given base of triangle and its height is 15 cm and 12 cm respectively Area of first triangle : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{1}{2} \times {\text{Base}} \times {\text{Height}} \\ & = \frac{1}{2} \times 15 \times 12 \\ & = 90{\text{ sq}}{\text{. cm}} \end{aligned}$$ According to the question, Let height of triangle be h cm Area of new triangle = 180 sq. cm Base = 20 sq. cm $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 180 = \frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times {\text{Height}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{h}} = \frac{{2 \times 180}}{{20}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{h}} = 18{\text{ cm}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The difference between the length and breadth of a rectangle is 23 m. If its perimeter is 206 m, then its area is :
s: We have : (l - b) = 23 and 2(l + b) = 206 or (l + b) = 103 Solving the two equations, we get : l = 63 and b = 40 ∴ Area = (l × b) = (63 × 40)m 2 = 2520 m 2

q: The length of a rectangle is three times of its width. If the length of the diagonal is $$8\sqrt {10}$$ cm, then the perimeter of the rectangle is :
s: Let breadth = x cm Then, length = 3x cm $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow {x^2} + {\left( {3x} \right)^2} = {\left( {8\sqrt {10} } \right)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow 10{x^2} = 640 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} = 64 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 8 \end{aligned}$$ So, length = 24 cm and breadth = 8 cm ∴ Perimeter = [2(24 + 8)] cm = 64 cm

q: A typist uses a paper 30 cm by 15 cm. He leaves a margin of 2.5 cm at the top and bottom and 1.25 cm on either side. What percentage of paper area is approximately available for typing ?
s: Area of the sheet = (30 × 15) cm 2 = 450 cm 2 Area used for typing = [(30 - 5) × (15 - 2.5)] cm 2 = 312.5 cm 2 ∴ Required percentage : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{312.5}}{{450}} \times 100} \right)\% \\ & = 69.4\% \approx 70\% \end{aligned}$$

q: The adjoining figure contains three squares with areas of 100, 16 and 49 lying side by side as shown. By how much should the area of the middle square be reduced in order that the total length PQ of the resulting three squares is 19 ?
s: PQ = $$\sqrt {100}$$ + $$\sqrt {16}$$ + $$\sqrt {49}$$ = (10 + 4 + 7) = 21 Side of middle square = $$\sqrt {16}$$ = 4 Reduction in PQ = (21 - 19) = 2 New side of middle square = (4 - 2) = 2 ∴ Reduction in area of middle square = (4 2 - 2 2 ) = 12

q: The three sides of a triangular field are 20 metres, 21 metres and 29 metres long respectively. The area of the field is :
s: Since (20) 2 + (21) 2 = (29) 2 So, it is a right-angled triangle with base = 20 m and height = 21 m ∴ Area = $$\left( {\frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 21} \right)$$ m 2 = 210 m 2

q: The diagonal of a square is $$4\sqrt 2$$ cm. The diagonal of another square whose area is double that of the first square, is :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & d = 4\sqrt 2 \,cm \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{Area }} = \frac{1}{2}d_1^2 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \frac{1}{2} \times {\left( {4\sqrt 2 } \right)^2} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{ = 16}}\,{\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \end{aligned}$$ Area of new square = (2 × 16) cm 2 = 32 cm 2 $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{1}{2}d_2^2 = 32 \\ & \Rightarrow d_2^2 = 64 \\ & \Rightarrow {d_2} = 8\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: What will be the area of 4 metres high wall on all four sides of a rectangular hall having perimeter 64 m ?
s: Perimeter = 64 m ⇒ 2(l + b) = 64 ∴ Area of 4 walls = 2(l + b) × h = (64 × 4) m 2 = 256 m 2

q: The altitude of an equilateral triangle of side $$2\sqrt 3$$ cm is :
s: Let ABC be the equilateral triangle and AD be the altitude on base BC In an equilateral triangle, the altitude and the median coincide. So, BC = DC = $$\left( {\frac{{2\sqrt 3 }}{2}} \right)$$ cm = $$\sqrt 3$$ cm Let the length of the altitude AD be x cm Then, in right angled ∆ADB, AB 2 = AD 2 + BD 2 ⇒ $${\left( {2\sqrt 3 } \right)^2}$$ = x 2 + $${\left( {\sqrt 3 } \right)^2}$$ ⇒ x 2 = (12 - 3) ⇒ x 2 = 9 ⇒ x = 3 cm

q: One of the diagonals of a rhombus is double the other diagonal. Its area is 25 sq. cm. The sum of the diagonal is ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{1}{2}{d_1} \times 2{d_1} = 25 \\ & \Leftrightarrow d_1^2 = 25 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {d_1} = 5 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Sum of lengths of diagonals = (5 + 10) cm = 15 cm

q: Cost of fencing a circular plot at the rate of Rs. 15 per metre is Rs. 3300. What will be the cost of flooring the plot at the rate of Rs. 100 per square metre ?
s: Circumference of the plot : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{3300}}{{15}}} \right)m \\ & = 220\,m \\ & \Rightarrow 2\pi R = 220 \\ & \Rightarrow R = \frac{{220 \times 7}}{{2 \times 22}} \\ & \Rightarrow R = 35\,m \end{aligned}$$ Area of the plot : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times 35 \times 35} \right){m^2} \\ & = 3850\,{m^2} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Cost of flooring : $$\begin{aligned} & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {3850 \times 100} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. 385000}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The ratio of the circumferences of two circles is 2 : 3. What is the ratio of their areas ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{{2\pi {R_1}}}{{2\pi {R_2}}} = \frac{2}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{{R_1}}}{{{R_2}}} = \frac{2}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{\pi R_1^2}}{{\pi R_2^2}} = {\left( {\frac{2}{3}} \right)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{\pi R_1^2}}{{\pi R_2^2}} = \frac{4}{9} \text{ or } 4:9 \end{aligned}$$

q: A circular road runs around a circular garden. If the difference between the circumference of the outer circle and the inner circle is 44 m, the width of the road is :
s: Let the radii of the outer and inner circle be R and r respectively Then, $$\begin{aligned} & 2\pi R - 2\pi r = 44 \\ & \Rightarrow 2\pi \left( {R - r} \right) = 44 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {R - r} \right) = \frac{{44 \times 7}}{{22 \times 2}} \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {R - r} \right) = 7 \end{aligned}$$

q: The area of the greatest circle which can be inscribed in a square whose perimeter is 120 cm, is :
s: Side of the square : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{120}}{4}cm \\ & = 30\,cm \end{aligned}$$ Radius of the required circle : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{1}{2} \times 30} \right)cm \\ & = 15\,cm \\ & = \pi \times {r^2} \\ & = \left[ {\frac{{22}}{7} \times {{\left( {15} \right)}^2}} \right]c{m^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: The area of the largest triangle that can be inscribed in a semi-circle of radius r, is :
s: Required area : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{1}{2} \times {\text{Base}} \times {\text{Height}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{1}{2} \times 2r \times r} \right) \\ & = {r^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: If radius of a circle is 3 cm, what is the area of the circle in sq. cm ?
s: Given: Radius of a circle = 3 cm Area of circle : $$\begin{aligned} & = \pi {r^2} \\ & = \pi \times {3^2} \\ & = 9\pi {\text{ sq}}{\text{.}}\,{\text{cm}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The base of an isosceles is 14 cm and its perimeter is 36 cm. Find its area.
s: Let each equal side of isosceles triangle be x cm Perimeter of an isosceles triangle = 36 cm $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore x + x + 14 = 36 \\ & \Rightarrow 2x = 36 - 14 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{22}}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 11\,cm \end{aligned}$$ BD = DC = 7cm From ∆ABD By using Pythagoras theorem : $$\begin{aligned} & AD = \sqrt {A{B^2} - B{D^2}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \sqrt {{{11}^2} - {7^2}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \sqrt {121 - 49} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \sqrt {72} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 3 \times 2\sqrt 2 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 6\sqrt 2 \,cm \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Area of ∆ABC $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{1}{2} \times BC \times AD \\ & = \frac{1}{2} \times 14 \times 6\sqrt 2 \\ & = 42\sqrt 2 {\text{ sq}}{\text{. cm}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The total cost of flooring a room at Rs. 8.50 per square metre is Rs. 510. If the length of the room is 8 m, its breadth is :
s: Area of the floor : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{510}}{{8.50}}} \right){m^2} \\ & = 60\,{m^2} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Breadth of the room : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{60}}{8}} \right)m \\ & = 7.5\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: The diagonal of a rectangular field is 15 metres and the difference between its length its length and width is 3 metres. The area of the rectangular field is :
s: Let l and b be the length and breadth of the rectangle respectively. Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \sqrt {{l^2} + {b^2}} = 15 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {{l^2} + {b^2}} \right) = {\left( {15} \right)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow {l^2} + {b^2} = 225 \end{aligned}$$ And, $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow l + b = 3 \\ & \Rightarrow {\left( {l - b} \right)^2} = 9 \\ & \Rightarrow {l^2} + {b^2} - 2lb = 9 \\ & \Rightarrow 225 - 2lb = 9 \\ & \Rightarrow 2lb = 216 \\ & \Rightarrow lb = 108 \end{aligned}$$ Hence, area of the field $$= lb = 108\,{m^2}$$

q: A room 5m × 8 m is to be carpeted leaving a margin of 10 cm from each wall. If the cost of the carpet is Rs. 18 per sq. meter, the cost of carpeting the room will be :
The length of a rectangular plot is thrice its breadth. If the area of the rectangular plot is 7803 sq. mtr, what is the breadth of the rectangular plot ?
s: Let the breadth of the plot be x metres Then, length of the plot = (3x) metres x × 3x = 7803 ⇒ 3x 2 = 7803 ⇒ x 2 = 2601 ⇒ x = $$\sqrt {2601}$$ ⇒ x = 51 m

q: A coaching institute wants to execute tiling work for one of its teaching halls 60 m long and 40 m wide with a square tile of 0.4 m side. If each tile costs Rs. 5, the total cost of tiles would be :
s: Number of tiles required : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{{\text{Area of hall}}}}{{{\text{Area of each tile}}}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{60 \times 40}}{{0.4 \times 0.4}}} \right) \\ & = 15000 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Total cost of tiles : = Rs. (15000 × 5) = Rs. 75000

q: The ratio of the area of a square to that of the square drawn on diagonal is :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Required ratio}} \\ & = \frac{{{a^2}}}{{{{\left( {\sqrt 2 a} \right)}^2}}} \\ & = \frac{{{a^2}}}{{2{a^2}}} \\ & = \frac{1}{2} \\ & = 1:2 \end{aligned}$$

q: The area of the four walls of a room is 120 m 2 and the length is twice the breadth. If the height of the room is 4 m, then the area of the floor is :
s: Let the breadth = x metres and length = (2x) metres Area of 4 walls = [2(2x + x)× 4] m 2 = (24x) m 2 ∴ 24x = 120 ⇒ x = 5 So, length = 10 m, and breadth = 5 m Area of the floor = (10 × 5) m 2 = 50 m 2

q: The perimeter of an isosceles triangle is equal to 14 cm and the lateral side is to the base in the ratio 5 : 4. The area of the triangle is :
s: Let the sides of the triangle be 5x, 5x and 4x cm respectively Then, 5x + 5x = 4x + 14 ⇒ 14 x = 14 ⇒ x = 1 So, a = 5 cm, b = 5 cm, c = 4 cm $$\begin{aligned} & s = \frac{{{\text{a + b + c}}}}{2} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \left( {\frac{{14}}{2}} \right)cm \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 7cm \end{aligned}$$ (s - a) = 2 cm, (s - b) = 2 cm, (s - c) = 3 cm ∴ Area of the triangle : $$\begin{aligned} & = \sqrt {7 \times 2 \times 2 \times 3} \\ & = 2\sqrt {21} \,c{m^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: The areas of two equilateral triangles are in the ratio 25 : 36. Their altitudes will be in the ratio :
s: Let the length of sides of the two triangles be a 1 and a 2 respectively and their altitudes be h 1 and h 2 respectively. Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{\frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{4}a_1^2}}{{\frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{4}a_2^2}} = \frac{{25}}{{36}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\left( {\frac{{{a_1}}}{{{a_2}}}} \right)^2} = {\left( {\frac{5}{6}} \right)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{{a_1}}}{{{a_2}}} = \frac{5}{6} \end{aligned}$$ And $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{\frac{1}{2} \times {a_1} \times {h_1}}}{{\frac{1}{2} \times {a_2} \times {h_2}}} = \frac{{25}}{{36}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{5}{6} \times \frac{{{h_1}}}{{{h_2}}} = \frac{{25}}{{36}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{{h_1}}}{{{h_2}}} = \frac{{25}}{{36}} \times \frac{6}{5} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{{h_1}}}{{{h_2}}} = \frac{5}{6} \end{aligned}$$

q: A diagonal of a rhombus is 6 cm. If its area is 24 cm 2 then the length of each side of the rhombus is :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times d = 24 \\ & \Rightarrow d = \frac{{24}}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow d = 8\,cm \\ & OA = 4\,cm\,{\text{and}}\,OB = 3\,cm \\ & \therefore AB = \sqrt {{{\left( {OA} \right)}^2} + {{\left( {OB} \right)}^2}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \sqrt {{4^2} + {3^2}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 5\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: The magnitude of the area of a circle is seven times that of its circumference. What is the circumference (in units) of the circle ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \pi {R^2} = 7 \times \left( {2\pi R} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow R = 14 \\ & \therefore {\text{ Circumference :}} \\ & {\text{= }}\left( {2 \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times 14} \right)\text{units} \\ & = 88\,\text{units} \end{aligned}$$

q: A small disc of radius r is cut out from a disc of radius R. The weight of the disc which now has a hole in it, is reduced to $$\frac{{24}}{{25}}$$ of the original weight. If R = xr, what is the value of x ?
s: Since weight of the disc is proportional to its area, we have : $$\begin{aligned} & \pi \left( {{R^2} - {r^2}} \right) = \frac{{24}}{{25}}\pi {R^2} \\ & \Rightarrow {R^2} - {r^2} = \frac{{24}}{{25}}{R^2} \\ & \Rightarrow {r^2} = \frac{1}{{25}}{R^2} \\ & \Rightarrow {R^2} = 25{r^2} \\ & \Rightarrow R = 5r \end{aligned}$$

q: The area of the largest circle, that can be drawn inside a rectangle with side 18 cm by 14 cm, is :
s: Radius of the required circle : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{1}{2} \times 14} \right)cm \\ & = 7\,cm \end{aligned}$$ Area of the circle : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times 7 \times 7} \right)\,c{m^2} \\ & = 154\,c{m^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: If the radius of a circle is increased by 75%, then its circumference will increase by :
s: Let original radius be R cm Then, original circumference = $$2\pi r$$ cm New radius : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {175\% {\text{ of }}R} \right)cm \\ & = \left( {\frac{{175}}{{100}} \times R} \right)cm \\ & = \frac{{7R}}{4}\,cm \end{aligned}$$ New circumference : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {2\pi \times \frac{{7R}}{4}} \right)cm \\ & = \frac{{7\pi R}}{2}\,cm \end{aligned}$$ Increase in circumference : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{7\pi R}}{2} - 2\pi R} \right)cm \\ & = \frac{{3\pi R}}{2}\,cm \end{aligned}$$ Increase % : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{3\pi R}}{2} \times \frac{1}{{2\pi R}} \times 100} \right)\% \\ & = 75\% \end{aligned}$$

q: A plate on square base made of brass is of length x cm and width 1 mm. The plate weights 4725 gm. If 1 cubic cm cm of brass weight 8.4 grams, then the value of x is :
s: Given length and width of a square base plate of brass is x cm and 1 mm Volume of the plate of square base = Area of base × height $$\begin{aligned} & = {x^2} \times \frac{1}{{10}} \\ & = \frac{{{x^2}}}{{10}}\,cu.cm. \end{aligned}$$ According to the question, $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{{{x^2}}}{{10}} \times 8.4 = 4725 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} = \frac{{4725 \times 10}}{{8.4}} \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} = 5625 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \sqrt {5625} = 75\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: What would be the area of a rectangle whose area is equal to the area of a circle of radius 7 cm ?
s: Radius of circle = 7cm Given area of rectangle : = Area of circle = $${\frac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7}$$ = 154 cm 2

q: The perimeter of a rectangle is 60 metres. If its length is twice its breadth, then its area is :
s: Let the breadth of the rectangle be x metres Then, length of the rectangle = 2x metres ⇒ 2(2x + x) = 60 ⇒ 6x = 60 ⇒ x = 10 So, length = 20 m, breadth = 10 m ∴ Area = (20 × 10) m 2 = 200 m 2

q: The diagonal of a rectangle is $$\sqrt {41}$$ cm and its area is 20 sq. cm. The perimeter of the rectangle must be :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \sqrt {{l^2} + {b^2}} = \sqrt {41} \\ & \Rightarrow {l^2} + {b^2} = 41 \\ & Also,\,\,lb = 20 \\ & {\left( {l + b} \right)^2} = \left( {{l^2} + {b^2}} \right) + 2lb \\ & {\left( {l + b} \right)^2} = 41 + 40 \\ & {\left( {l + b} \right)^2} = 81 \\ & \left( {l + b} \right) = 9 \\ & \therefore {\text{ Perimeter}} = 2\left( {l + b} \right) = 18\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: The breadth of a rectangular field is $$\frac{3}{4}$$ of its length and its area is 300 sq. metres. What will be the area (in sq. metres) of the garden of breath 1.5 metres developed around the field ?
s: Let the length of the field be x metres Then, breadth of the field = $$\frac{3x}{4}$$ metres $$\begin{aligned} & x \times \frac{{3x}}{4} = 300 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} = 300 \times \frac{4}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} = 400 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 20 \end{aligned}$$ So, length = 20 m, breadth = 15 m ∴ Area of the garden : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {\left\{ {\left( {20 + 3} \right) \times \left( {15 + 3} \right)} \right\} - \left( {20 \times 15} \right)} \right]{m^2} \\ & = \left[ {\left( {23 \times 18} \right) - \left( {20 \times 15} \right)} \right]{m^2} \\ & = \left( {414 - 300} \right){m^2} \\ & = 114\,{m^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: How many squares with side $$\frac{1}{2}$$ inch long are needed to cover a rectangle that is 4 feet long and 6 feet wide ?
s: length of rectangle = 4ft = (4 ×12) inch = 48 inch length of rectangle = 6ft = (6 ×12) inch = 72 inch ∴ Number of squares : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{48 \times 72}}{{\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2}}} \\ & = 13824 \end{aligned}$$

q: If a square of area $$\frac{\text{A}}{2}$$ is cut off from a given square of area A, then the ratio of diagonal of the cut off square to that of the given square is :
s: Let the length of diagonal of the bigger square be x and that of the smaller square be y. Then, $$A = \frac{1}{2}{x^2}\,\,or\,\,x = \sqrt {2A}$$ And, $$\frac{A}{2} = \frac{1}{2}{y^2}\,\,or\,\,y = \sqrt A$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ Required ratio :}} \\ & = \frac{y}{x} = \frac{{\sqrt A }}{{\sqrt {2A} }} = 1:\sqrt 2 {\text{ }} \end{aligned}$$

q: The length of a room is double its breadth. The cost of colouring the ceiling at Rs. 25 per sq. meter is Rs. 5000 and the cost of painting the four walls at Rs. 240 per sq. metre is Rs. 64800. Find the height of the room :
s: Let the breadth and height of the room be b metres and h metres respectively. Then, length of the room = (2b) metres Area of the ceiling : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {2b \times b} \right)m \\ & = \left( {2{b^2}} \right){m^2} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & 2{b^2} = \frac{{5000}}{{25}} \\ & 2{b^2} = 200 \\ & {b^2} = 100 \\ & b = 10 \end{aligned}$$ So, length = 20 m, breadth = 10 m Area of 4 walls : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {2\left( {20 + 10} \right) \times h} \right]{m^2} \\ & = \left( {60h} \right){m^2} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 60h = \frac{{64800}}{{240}} \\ & \Rightarrow 60h = 270 \\ & \Rightarrow h = \frac{{270}}{{60}} \\ & \Rightarrow h = 4.5\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: The sides of a triangle are in ratio of $$\frac{1}{2}:\frac{1}{3}:\frac{1}{4}$$ . If the perimeter is 52 cm, then the length of the smallest side is :
s: Ratio of sides = $$\frac{1}{2}:\frac{1}{3}:\frac{1}{4}$$ = 6 : 4 : 3 Perimeter = 52 cm So, sides are : $$\begin{aligned} & \left( {52 \times \frac{6}{{13}}} \right)cm \\ & \left( {52 \times \frac{4}{{13}}} \right)cm\,\& \\ & \left( {52 \times \frac{3}{{13}}} \right)cm \end{aligned}$$ So, a = 24 cm, b = 16 cm, and c = 12 cm ∴ Length of smallest side = 12 cm

q: If x is the length of a median of an equilateral triangle, then its area is :
s: Let the side of the triangle be a Then, $$\begin{aligned} & {a^2} = {\left( {\frac{a}{2}} \right)^2} + {x^2} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{3{a^2}}}{4} = {x^2} \\ & \Leftrightarrow {a^2} = \frac{{4{x^2}}}{3} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Area : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{4}{a^2} \\ & = \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{4} \times \frac{{4{x^2}}}{3} \\ & = \frac{{{x^2}}}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & = \frac{{\sqrt 3 {x^2}}}{3} \end{aligned}$$

q: If a square and a rhombus stand on the same base, then the ratio of the areas of the square and the rhombus is :
s: A square and a rhombus on the same base are equal in area.

q: Two small circular parks of diameters 16 m and 12 m are to be replaced by a Bigger circular park. What would be the radius of this new park. If the new park has to occupy the same space as the two small parks ?
s: Let the radius of the new park be R m Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \pi {R^2} = \pi \times {8^2} + \pi \times {6^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \pi {R^2} = 100\pi \\ & \Rightarrow {R^2} = 100 \\ & \Rightarrow R = 10 \end{aligned}$$

q: If the wheel of the engine of a train $$4\frac{2}{7}$$ metres in circumference makes 7 revolutions in 4 seconds, then the speed (in km/hr) of the train is :
s: Distance covered in 4 sec : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{30}}{7} \times 7} \right)m \\ & = 30\,m \end{aligned}$$ Distance covered in 1 sec = $$\frac{{30}}{4}$$ Distance covered in 1 revolution : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{30}}{4}} \right)m \\ & = \frac{{15}}{2}m \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Required speed : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{15}}{2}} \right)m/s \\ & = \left( {\frac{{15}}{2} \times \frac{{18}}{5}} \right)km/hr \\ & = 27\,km/hr \end{aligned}$$

q: A circular swimming pool is surrounded by a concrete wall 4 ft. wide. If the area of the concrete wall surrounding the pool is $$\frac{{11}}{{25}}$$ that of the pool, then the radius of the pool is :
s: Let the radius of the pool be R ft. Radius of the pool including the wall = (R + 4)ft. Area of the concrete wall : $$\begin{aligned} & = \pi \left[ {{{\left( {R + 4} \right)}^2} - {R^2}} \right]sq.ft \\ & = \pi \left[ {\left( {R + 4 + R} \right)\left( {R + 4 - R} \right)} \right]sq.ft \\ & = 8\pi \left( {R + 2} \right)sq.ft \\ & 8\pi \left( {R + 2} \right) = \frac{{11}}{{25}}\pi {R^2} \\ & \Rightarrow 11{R^2} = 200\left( {R + 2} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow 11{R^2} - 200R - 400 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow 11{R^2} - 220R + 20R - 400 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow 11R\left( {R - 20} \right) + 20\left( {R - 20} \right) = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {R - 20} \right)\left( {11R + 20} \right) = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow R = 20 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Radius of the pool = 20 ft.

q: The sides of a rectangle are 8 cm and 6 cm. The corners of the rectangle lie on a circle. Find the are a of the circle without the rectangle :
s: Diameter of the circle : $$\begin{aligned} & = AC = \sqrt {{{\left( {AB} \right)}^2} + {{\left( {BC} \right)}^2}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \sqrt {{8^2} + {6^2}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = \sqrt {100} \,cm \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 10\,cm \end{aligned}$$ Radius = 5 cm Required area = (Area of the circle) - (Area of the rectangle) $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {\left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times 5 \times 5} \right) - \left( {8 \times 6} \right)} \right]c{m^2} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{550}}{7} - 48} \right)c{m^2} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{214}}{7}} \right)c{m^2} \\ & = 30.57\,c{m^2} \approx 30.6\,c{m^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: A can go round a circular path 8 times in 40 minutes. If the diameter of the circle is increased to 10 times the original diameter, then the time required by A to go round the new path once, travelling at the same speed as before, is :
s: Let original diameter be d metre Then, its circumference = $$\left( {\pi d} \right)$$ metres Time taken to cover $$\left( {8\pi d} \right)$$ m = 40 min New diameter = $$\left( {10d} \right)$$ m Then, its circumference = $$\left( {\pi \times 10d} \right)$$ m ∴ Time taken to go round it once : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{40}}{{8\pi d}} \times 10\pi d} \right)\min \\ & = 50\,\min \end{aligned}$$

q: Area of a rectangle is 150 sq. metre. When the breadth of the same rectangle is increased by 2 metres and the length decreased by 5 metres the area of the rectangle decreases by 30 square metres. What is the perimeter of the square whose sides are equal to the length of the rectangle ?
s: Let the length of rectangle be $$l$$ metre and the breadth of the rectangle be $$b$$ metre Then area of the rectangle = $$l$$ × $$b$$ $$lb$$ = 150 m 2 . . . . . (i) According to the question, $$\begin{aligned} & \left( {l - 5} \right) \times \left( {b + 2} \right) = 150 - 30 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {l - 5} \right) \times \left( {b + 2} \right) = 120 \\ & \Rightarrow lb - 5b + 2l - 10 = 120 \\ & \Rightarrow 150 - 5b + 2l - 10 = 120 \\ & \Rightarrow 5b - 2l = 20 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{5 \times 150}}{l} - 2{l^2} = 20l \\ & \Rightarrow 2{l^2} + 20l - 750 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow {l^2} + 10l - 375 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow l\left( {l + 25} \right) - 15\left( {l + 25} \right) = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {l + 15} \right)\left( {l + 25} \right) = 0 \end{aligned}$$ On solving both equations we get, $$l$$ = 15 m and $$b$$ = 10 m Side of square = length of rectangle (given) So, the perimeter of the square : = 4 × $$l$$ = 4 × 15 = 60 m

q: If the total surface area of a cube is 864 square cm, find the volume of the cube ?
s: Each edges of cube = a cm ∴ Total surface area of cube = 6a 2 ⇒ 6a 2 = 864 ⇒ a 2 = $$\frac{864}{6}$$ = 144 ⇒ a = $$\sqrt {144}$$ = 12 cm ∴ Volume of cube : = a 3 cm 3 = (12 × 12 × 12) cm 3 = 1728 cm 3

q: A man is walking in a rectangular field whose perimeter is 6 km. If the area of the rectangular field be 2 sq. km, then what is the difference between the length and breadth of the rectangle ?
s: Let the length and breadth of the field be l and b km respectively Then, 2 (l + b) = 6 ⇒ l + b = 3 And lb = 2 (l - b) 2 = (l + b) 2 - 4lb ⇒ (l - b) 2 = 3 2 - 4 × 2 ⇒ (l - b) 2 = 1 ⇒ (l - b) = 1 km

q: If the diagonal and the area of a rectangle are 25 m 2 and 168 m 2 , what is the length of the rectangle ?
s: Let the length of the rectangle be x metres. Then, breath of the rectangle = $$\left( {\frac{{168}}{x}} \right)m$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \sqrt {{x^2} + {{\left( {\frac{{168}}{x}} \right)}^2}} = 25 \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt {{x^2} + \frac{{28224}}{{{x^2}}}} = 25 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} + \frac{{28224}}{{{x^2}}} = 625 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^4} - 625{x^2} + 28224 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^4} - 576{x^2} - 49{x^2} + 28224 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2}\left( {{x^2} - 576} \right) - 49\left( {{x^2} - 576} \right) = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {{x^2} - 576} \right)\left( {{x^2} - 49} \right) = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} = 576\,\,or\,\,{x^2} = 49 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 24\,\,\,or\,\,\,x = 7 \end{aligned}$$ Hence, length = 24 m and breadth = 7 m

q: A path of uniform width runs round the inside of a rectangular field 38 m long 32 m wide. If the path occupies 600 m 2 , then the width of the path is :
s: Let the width of the path be x Then, $$\left[ {\left( {38 \times 32} \right) - \left\{ {\left( {38 - 2x} \right)\left( {32 - 2x} \right)} \right\}} \right]$$ $$= 600$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \left[ {1216 - \left( {1216 - 140x + 4{x^2}} \right)} \right] \\ & \Rightarrow 4{x^2} - 140x + 600 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} - 35x + 150 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} - 30x - 5x + 150 = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \left( {x - 30} \right)\left( {x - 5} \right) = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 5\,m\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\left[ {\therefore x \ne 30} \right] \end{aligned}$$

q: The length and breadth of the floor of the room are 20 feet and 10 feet respectively. Square tiles of 2 feet length of different colours are to be laid on the floor. Black tiles are laid in the first row on all sides. If white tiles are laid in the one-third of the remaining and blue tiles in the rest, how many blue tiles will be there ?
s: Area left after laying black tiles : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {\left( {20 - 4} \right) \times \left( {10 - 4} \right)} \right]{\text{sq}}{\text{.ft.}} \\ & = 96\,{\text{sq}}{\text{.ft.}} \end{aligned}$$ Area under white tiles : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{1}{3} \times 96} \right){\text{sq}}{\text{.ft.}} \\ & = 32\,{\text{sq}}{\text{.ft.}} \end{aligned}$$ Area under blue tiles : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {96 - 32} \right){\text{sq}}{\text{.ft.}} \\ & = 64\,{\text{sq}}{\text{.ft.}} \end{aligned}$$ Number of blue tiles : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{64}}{{\left( {2 \times 2} \right)}} \\ & = 16 \end{aligned}$$

q: Of the two square fields, the area of one is 1 hectare while the other one is broader by 1%. The difference in their areas is :
s: Area = 1 hect. = 10000 sq. m Side = $$\sqrt {10000}$$ m = 100 m Side of the other square = 101 m Difference in their areas : = [(101) 2 - (100) 2 ] m 2 = [(101 + 100) (101 - 100)] m 2 = 201 m 2
